newsitem.title: USA: Fire extinguished at PSE&G NJ substation.
newsitem.headline: Fire extinguished at PSE&G NJ substation.

text.p: Firefighters have extinguished a blaze at the Public Service Electric and Gas (PSE&G) Bayway power substation in Elizabeth, N.J., a company spokesman said Friday.
"The fire is out, but it's still very hot. They're laying down foam on it now," said PSE&G spokesman Fran Sullivan.
"We hope to have our people in the facility in the next couple of hours to assess the damage," he said.

The Newark-based utility said it was still rerouting power around the damaged substation, and that about 35,000 customers in Elizabeth, a port city on the southwest side of New York harbor, were still without electricity.
PSE&G said it is still unable to supply a full load of power to the nearby Newark International Airport, which is making up the loss using backup power from its own generators, Sullivan said.
"But there are flight delays, so we're telling everyone to check with their carrier before heading to the airport," he said.
The airport, a major hub for air traffic to the greater New York-New Jersey metropolitan area, handles on average about 1,235 flights a day.
The cause of the fire, which broke out about 0530 EDT/0930 GMT, was not yet known, though a local fire official told Reuters it appeared to have been caused by an exploding transformer.
PSE&G, based in Newark, N.J., is a subsidiary of Public Service Enterprise Inc.
